assumptions: The initial market is Poland and the product remains a voluntary B2B2C financial-wellbeing feature, with no gambling-operator funding, adverse decisioning, diagnosis, or clinical-treatment claim.
Live account access is supplied by a registered AISP and enrichment partner rather than through the founder obtaining an AISP registration during initial validation.

A counsel-reviewed purpose, role allocation, consent flow, DPIA, retention policy, and withdrawal behavior can in principle make the narrow workflow lawful; this is unresolved rather than presumed impossible.
The founder begins part-time with approximately PLN 70,000 and uses qualified legal, security, and support partners for work that AI or software cannot substitute.
The proposed prices, margins, user scale, renewals, and valuation path are planning hypotheses rather than observed economics.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The concept correctly identifies a real gap between a one-time native gambling block and a voluntary longitudinal workflow combining guardrails, user corrections, and support export. However, the evidence does not yet show that this workflow is a distinct high-value job rather than a feature extension of controls and transaction labels that incumbents already provide.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Problem gambling can create severe consumer harm, and Polish prevalence data establish a nontrivial affected population. The proposed payer's pain is much less clear: no named budget owner, paid pilot, or purchasing evidence exists, most gamblers in the cited study were classified as safe, and free native controls give institutions a credible low-cost response.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Recurring platform and active-user fees could eventually produce attractive software economics, but every material input is unverified. Proposed pricing, 65-80% gross margin, 12-24 month payback, renewal behavior, support burden, and the route to 150,000 paid active users lack evidence; AISP fees, security reviews, compliance, integration work, insurance, and incident readiness can make early deployments service-heavy and cash-inefficient.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish gambling activity and the documented harm population make the underlying use case meaningful, but transaction volume is not product revenue and the serviceable paying market is undefined. Banks, fintechs, employee-assistance programs, and debt-support organizations have different budgets and workflows, so the current beachhead is too diffuse to demonstrate a narrow, economically sufficient entry segment.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Banks and fintechs own the customer relationship, account context, and distribution, while Revolut demonstrates that a Polish-facing institution can offer a free native block and Kontomatik already supplies gambling categorization. A new vendor could become an embedded specialist, but it presently has neither exclusive access, outcome proof, nor a proprietary capability strong enough to support segment leadership.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A trusted consent-and-guardrail workflow could extend to other geographies, support providers, or voluntary financial-wellbeing behaviors. Those adjacencies are plausible but not automatically unlocked: each may require new sensitive-data purposes, intervention evidence, integrations, and buyer approval, while expansion into adverse or diagnostic uses is intentionally unavailable.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Long-lived integrations, auditable consent operations, user-corrected labels, and ethically measured outcomes could compound into a useful workflow asset. At present they are proposed future advantages; categorization is already available, consent UX is reproducible, raw account data are purpose-limited and non-transferable, and distributors can build or switch suppliers.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The offer is broader than a simple block, but no measured improvement in user outcomes, classification coverage, engagement, counselor efficiency, compliance burden, or cost has been established. Without a large and demonstrable improvement on native blocks and established enrichment, asking users and institutions to accept extra consent, monitoring, integration, and privacy risk is difficult.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Open-banking infrastructure, visible gambling activity, and demonstrated use of blocking features make experimentation timely. The same timing has also enabled established vendors and banks to ship substitutes, while PSD2 purpose limits and GDPR special-category risk raise the adoption bar rather than creating a clear regulatory tailwind.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Embedding through institutions is directionally sensible and avoids costly, ethically fraught direct acquisition of vulnerable consumers. Yet no channel commitment or buyer access is shown, enterprise sales and security procurement are likely long, each integration may be bespoke, and the same institutions that control reach can provide a native feature or buy categorization from an incumbent.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data-science skills, personal domain familiarity, AI leverage, and a synthetic-data prototype fit a part-time start. Live execution nevertheless depends on legal role design, explicit consent where required, AISP contractual permission, secure processing, high classification accuracy across difficult payment rails, safe false-positive handling, qualified support ownership, and enterprise procurement; the proposed time and capital may be insufficient once these obligations begin.

main_structural_strength: The concept can use institutional distribution and a registered AISP to deliver an opt-in, user-controlled safety workflow without requiring direct consumer acquisition or the founder to perform clinical care, while consent operations and measured outcomes could become more valuable with repeated deployments.
primary_score_limiter: The intended distributors are simultaneously the budget holders, customer gatekeepers, and strongest build-or-buy substitutes, yet there is no evidence that any of them values the incremental workflow enough to pay a price that supports the proposed economics.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Revolut already provides Polish customers a free gambling block and Kontomatik already supplies a Polish gambling-transaction label; together these show that both basic intervention and core categorization can be delivered by institutions or established infrastructure vendors without this product.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid design partnership with a named budget owner should establish an acceptable price and procurement path, followed by a counsel-approved live pilot that measures opt-in and consent persistence, precision and recall by payment rail, incremental benefit over a native block, support burden, total AISP and security cost, gross margin, and a renewal or expansion commitment.
highest_value_structural_change: Replace the broad bank-fintech-EAP API pitch with one counselor-led gambling-debt workflow for a specific debt-support or financial-wellbeing provider: let a contracted AISP own account access, let the qualified provider own intervention and crisis handling, and charge for measurable case-resolution or counselor-efficiency value rather than generic active users. This makes the buyer's operational pain and paid event concrete and shifts differentiation from commodity labeling toward an embedded outcome workflow.
